<li data-list-item-id="ef8e1fb309215786b79c6a3147983c2f2">(Optional) <code>search_str</code> – A search string to filter the returned values.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e04a3987b17faebe8e0812a98aa7f675c">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ee887dd05092f2e1f32edd38608df1ce9"><em>What values exist in the "country" column?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e399bd07eae37b6ea5acf6375bd44000e"><em>Show me all distinct values for the "plan type" property.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e3841288657370a529642f09f1dee378d"><em>Search for column values that start with "US" in the region field.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_find_datasets</code> – Searches and lists available datasets in Optimizely Analytics. It uses fuzzy matching on dataset names and semantic search on descriptions to find relevant datasets.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eacca46b74a2c51abc3132c3ab2852994">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e92c32ed607af3739d16d9bc6d93f9c5e">To locate specific datasets by name or keyword within Optimizely Analytics.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e93310fb990d1a24dcd71d39c5aadfcbf">To discover available datasets related to a particular topic or area of interest.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee254abf29bd96d6d84c153d5a23dbef5">To get a comprehensive list of all accessible datasets.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8f539ee1a1c26118f52ad6999cab1edb">To identify relevant datasets for further analysis or reporting.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e76c407a4c7881d1d1f20e2cb23f38734">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ece8699f8340d06d7d261fa60d4109cb7">
<code>query</code> – A natural language search query to filter datasets by name or description. For example, <code>mobile users</code>, <code>premium customers</code>, or <code>active subscribers</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2e6879b91c75e433f4c41ee773640344">(Optional) <code>appId</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7151e3f871fcab417664771387d343ed">(Optional) categories – A list of category IDs to filter results by. Use the  Use the <code>oa_list_categories</code> tool to discover available categories.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ecb74366e1b494cbea271c17643dbef16">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e5dcd2e7102ffc9252fe3eedb405f11ea"><em>Find datasets related to 'user behavior'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e083369b509f68ac4be60e273a232b340"><em>Show me all datasets.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ea49b7e27952b1f939cd26516dfd1de86"><em>What datasets can I use for my analysis?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ec5628a9ba00c0bb64616c0b295593014"><em>Are there any datasets about 'e-commerce sales'?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e7ca3eda7d1dbe28eacb40284a311f445"><em>Search for datasets containing 'product'.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_find_metrics</code> – Searches for saved metrics in Optimizely Analytics using fuzzy search on metric names and semantic search on descriptions.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eefdc7309610d52c6a55282eaf5a866df">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ef906b76cbf5c113fa0d0d5792d7dba4f">Locate a previously saved metric, like <code>revenue</code> or <code>conversion rate</code>, for use in an exploration or scorecard.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0a4a9e30c71ce07453d1954ddc380db9">Search for existing metrics by name or description to reference in an experiment scorecard.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb8c7941a9045f9e5239bc6797b03969c">Discover available metrics related to a specific business area, such as average order value or bounce rate.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e60f12c5133f6a7dacdbc9dae43179296">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e6eb04bcb69e054497bbfa1d2c125b2ee">
<code>query</code> – A natural language search query to find metrics (for example, <code>revenue</code>, <code>conversion rate</code>, or <code>average order value</code>). The search uses fuzzy matching on names and semantic matching on descriptions.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e62a5c8c75f84a8fbdd56891450d2d86b">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0930dc6b7bb182784e0dac9d8c786737">(Optional) <code>categories</code> – A list of category IDs to filter results by. When provided, only results that belong to at least one of the specified categories will be returned. Use the <code>oa_list_categories</code> tool to discover available categories and their IDs. Category filtering is handled entirely by this parameter. Do not include category names or references to categories in the <code>query</code> parameter. If the request is solely about filtering by category, use a broad <code>query</code> such as an empty string.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e01f0a40e99c1cbd8baa10ca2b82c6915">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e229f15877107b735fcc46c076e7e26c8"><em>Are there any saved metrics for conversion rate?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e7ac2cf7bbc828d3980702da0b9489b11"><em>Show me metrics related to average order value.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e58bd1eec585dc6c59de5ab0dde71b188"><em>Can you find the "daily active users" metric?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e6ad337918c3462fa7ca1f8f8032a09d1"><em>Search for metrics about revenue or purchases.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_get_metric_data</code> – Retrieves and executes a specific saved metric in Optimizely Analytics, returning its calculated table data.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eadcb4835f0f26c793bd41ad55f5be2a7">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ed6fd319105bd40df25e88d16237df83f">You want to see the actual data values for a metric you previously found using the <code>oa_find_metrics</code> tool. </li>
<li data-list-item-id="e64c4ee735e046678d5b0876e007edb1e">To analyze the trends or patterns for a specific metric over a defined period or granularity.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6e2589a6fc377ede33142857c77b46f9">You want to understand the performance of a key business indicator. </li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ec7debf3386a9dadc31103ca9bdfabcc5">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e92c41643620cf45d138fe7695b02964d">
<code>app_id</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2eac5f3927261aa99f029183e8929e7f">
<code>metric_id</code> – The ID of the specific metric to retrieve from the <code>oa_find_metrics</code> tool.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebc154729fd057ae9ee939d037b15935d">(Optional) <code>start_date</code> – The start date for the data retrieval in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. </li>
<li data-list-item-id="e44066f91b8e08546369f3d69b6b546f5">(Optional) <code>end_date</code> – The end date for the data retrieval in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e2e179aa92b362c199f07514c5e0f1d4b">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e387922f136bfbe26c9b234f7e77b8271">
<em>Get metric data for app </em><code><em>123</em></code><em> and metric </em><code><em>conversion_rate</em></code><em>.</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e9563fe005acc33920a8cf675bdecb905">
<em>Retrieve the </em><code><em>page_views</em></code><em> metric for application </em><code><em>456</em></code><em> from </em><code><em>2025-01-01</em></code><em> to </em><code><em>2025-01-31</em></code><em>.</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb41e11897b7bb6ec543890631d6ed142">
<em>What is the </em><code><em>bounce_rate</em></code><em> for app </em><code><em>789</em></code><em>?</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e0d3747cc7a2abfe15b839759fb0140e0">
<em>Show me the </em><code><em>revenue</em></code><em> metric for app </em><code><em>101</em></code><em> for the last week.</em>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_list_apps</code> – Lists all available applications in Optimizely Analytics.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e1512fd0042c8fed3644cc52913d27185">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e90bbcdb44e02850ec63a288b2d85f15d">To see all applications you have access to within Analytics.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e13a0d15545adb68b591135b796c95452">To find the ID of a specific application when you need to perform actions on it.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e66ad31cf7cc0934fbb8e730f5fd06cd3">To get an overview of your Optimizely Analytics application landscape and available projects.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e3cb348c86c00fbfa4e28ced2594e03dd">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="e3860493e5d08bb5e751892812cb1e682">None</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e43df0dfba49c677312bf5c49bba5f2f4">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed57501d5629ea7f132d191248bfb128e"><em>List all Optimizely applications.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e10623b79866ab8aacea755bc626deaf2"><em>What applications are available in Optimizely Analytics?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e799b5b54c48fd26aeba240493e83e591"><em>Show me a list of all apps I have access to.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_list_categories</code> – Lists all categories available in the current Optimizely Analytics application.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e25b6df63851198f6335eeb97c6255c0c">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e5697e40f3210a7d2b399503dcf2ab2c2">Discover available category IDs for use with the <code>categories</code> filter parameter in other search tools.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea151a00d6b456cc462196f5edc52f6f6">Filter search results for events, entities, datasets, explores, metrics, or dashboards by category.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e262c27f5f1d5ac04484be9e64f9443b2">Browse all categories to understand how your analytics data is organized.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ec8675b67fcb31cd2469987829f9f53d7">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul><li data-list-item-id="e3192bab7f82deb1f3955e4a89dbf3364">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li></ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea94daa98b23ed3781c5c6e08f4e44abd">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e9129365f55f7e159a126eff2f75452a5"><em>What categories are available in my analytics app?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e2d87fef328efdb7861e386206dee071e"><em>List all categories so I can filter my event search.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ef6eb7fbd0c6d8b9a44738b46fbabb6a9"><em>Show me the category IDs I can use to filter explorations.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><h2 id="h_01KVDT7960Y1YCKX6ZADDV7MQG">Data ingestion tools<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KVDT7960Y1YCKX6ZADDV7MQG"></a></h2><details><summary><code>oa_csv_upload</code> – Uploads Comma-Separated Values (CSV) data into a new or existing table in the app's data warehouse in Optimizely Analytics.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea3e398c20dfbb71e5e2a04d2c623200c">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ecbee409c10fdd8461c48f5baf6b5ce0c">Upload CSV content or load tabular data into the Optimizely Analytics data warehouse.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb21e9c94ccc9a727a049653844cf700a">Create a new table from a CSV file for use in explorations and analyses.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e541760d81148e262065e7f0ea974db30">Append new rows to an existing warehouse table or overwrite it with fresh data.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e3fb36c369407b172402472eb6f8dcd27">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e06a9ce4ff26c3034fc72de5421bdb3da">
<code>columns</code> – Array of column definitions. Each element must have <code>name</code> (string) and <code>type</code> (one of: <code>BOOL</code>, <code>DATE</code>, <code>DATETIME</code>, <code>DOUBLE</code>, <code>INT32</code>, <code>INT64</code>, <code>TIME</code>, or <code>VARCHAR</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3e1dcc7758acc57b0d1f7c1175d1b2cd">
<code>table_name</code> – The name for the destination table.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb9f9661908e839abeb84f767f96b63ab">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eaca74aff883f225ff0791f14c5fa95e7">(Optional) <code>csv_data</code> – The CSV file content, base64-encoded. Provide either <code>csv_data</code> or <code>file_url</code>. Maximum decoded size is 5 MB.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efbb119d6209d5492c69787fd2ba6331c">(Optional) <code>file_url</code> – URL of a CSV file to download. The file is fetched using the caller's access token. Provide either <code>file_url</code> or <code>csv_data</code>. Maximum file size is 20 MB.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0e853125dc1e678ef4b05668d0c4aa4e">(Optional) <code>write_mode</code> – How to handle existing data. Defaults to <code>CREATE</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee98400affce0fc92de55bec39a123cba">(Optional) <code>has_header</code> – Whether the first row of the CSV is a header row. If true, the header row is skipped during data loading. Defaults to <code>true</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee56d928e4d549228ceb00d0ab1d071bd">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ee79c63404d920841ac8fba286d1508af"><em>Upload this CSV file to a new table called "campaign_results" with columns: name (VARCHAR), revenue (DOUBLE), date (DATE).</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e180f140b70d8fb2431d6ba6a9bc0de8e">
<em>Load the CSV at </em><code><em>https://example.com/data.csv</em></code><em> into the warehouse as "user_events".</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ecf8d4638ea70907d4cf8d608b9e73031"><em>Overwrite the existing "orders" table with new data from my CSV.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e49fd4e85ba5fc783bae5e3eded47fd7c"><em>Append rows from this CSV to the "daily_metrics" table.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><h2 id="h_01KVDX4BZD3EGTATHF2SN01SVD">Exploration creation tools<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KVDX4BZD3EGTATHF2SN01SVD"></a></h2><details><summary><code>oa_analyze_explore</code> – Retrieves exploration data from Optimizely Analytics for analysis of existing saved explorations.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eb6be5ac07ee3a53dfa539c8f4e1d90f4">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="edee77b8c76193b21d15fc48e5f4568a8">Analyze a previously saved exploration to surface insights from its data.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed5477567a483db34fa094114b72680c3">Re-run a saved exploration with a different time range or time granularity.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e23e6a7d018c1b1ff4e78b0f79d81bed0">Apply ad-hoc filters or sampling overrides to a saved exploration without modifying it permanently.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef424bc07db45878922817f14ccbc2bc4">Analyze an exploration in the context of a dashboard, automatically applying the dashboard's always-on filters.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eb82dedeb2438eb60824fa7c649a8429e">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ef99e13122634ed13c5d5a3eb43abb26c">
<code>explore_id</code> – The unique identifier of a saved exploration (format: <code><number>_<uuid></code>). Must be obtained from the <code>id</code> field in the <code>oa_find_explores</code> tool response. Do not pass dashboard IDs, experiment IDs, or draft explore IDs here.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6db9c971c12cf8d9a89254cb9b5424e9">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2cda3ec05d10081393cdbe27c61feef3">(Optional) <code>time_range</code> – Overrides the time range for analyzing the exploration. The agent should intelligently include this parameter when the user specifies a different time period than the exploration's default. For example, <em>show me that exploration for the last month </em>or <em>re-run for January 2024 to January 2025</em>. The object must have either a <code>last</code> field for relative ranges or both <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> fields for absolute ranges: For relative ranges (for example, l<em>ast 30 days</em> or <em>past week</em>): <code>{ "last": { "value": 30, "unit": "DAY" } }</code> Valid units: <code>SECOND</code>, <code>MINUTE</code>, <code>HOUR</code>, <code>DAY</code>, <code>WEEK</code>, <code>MONTH</code>, <code>QUARTER</code>, <code>YEAR</code>, and <code>EON</code>. For "all time" or "ever" queries (for example, <em>how many users ever did X</em>): <code>{ "last": { "value": 1, "unit": "EON" } }</code> The <code>EON</code> unit represents all time from the beginning of data collection. For absolute ranges (for example, <em>January 2024 to January 2025</em>): <code>{ "start": "2024-01-01", "end": "2025-01-01" }</code> Date formats accepted: ISO-8601 dates (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS), dates with timezone (Z or +/- offset), or epoch milliseconds. Dates without timezone are interpreted in the application's configured timezone.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7641cd2000e88760cb17101c630040ce">(Optional) <code>time_grain</code> – Overrides the time granularity for the exploration data (for example, daily, weekly, or monthly). The agent should include this parameter when the user specifies a different time grouping than the exploration's default (for example, "show me monthly instead", "break it down by week", "daily granularity"). The object has two fields: <code>{ "value": <number>, "unit": "<UNIT>" }</code> Common examples: Daily: <code>{ "value": 1, "unit": "DAY" }</code>, Weekly: <code>{ "value": 1, "unit": "WEEK" }</code>, Monthly: <code>{ "value": 1, "unit": "MONTH" }</code>. Valid units: <code>SECOND</code>, <code>MINUTE</code>, <code>HOUR</code>, <code>DAY</code>, <code>WEEK</code>, <code>MONTH</code>, <code>QUARTER</code>, or <code>YEAR</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1ad06f6a21f6d62949ec4bfc4bb5c493">(Optional) <code>filters</code> – Filter overrides to apply at query time without saving the exploration. Use this for user-selectable dashboard filter tiles when the user specifies a value. Pass <code>column_id</code> and <code>operator</code> from the filter tile response plus the user's value. Also use for ad-hoc filtering outside a dashboard context. Do not use this for always-on filter tiles. Pass <code>dashboard_id</code> instead and the backend auto-applies them. Multiple filters are combined with and logic. Each filter object has teh following: <ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ed2f85e44c748081d9378b1d869e2a5f7">
<code>column_id</code> – An entity reference object with <code>entity_id</code> (string). The <code>entity_id</code> is the <code>id</code> field from an entity returned by the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool, and an optional <code>field_path</code> (string) that targets a JSON subfield using dot notation (for example, <code>"plan.name"</code> or <code>"revenue"</code>). Use <code>field_path</code> only when the entity is a JSON-typed column whose subfields you discovered with the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool. Examples: <code>{"entity_id": "433243659_b9115050-f9db-4564-8378-220c7a51d5d3"}</code>, <code>{"entity_id": "433243659_a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "field_path": "plan.name"}</code>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7eada81f584301e5e664df2bd7fc6aa8">
<code>operator</code> (string)  – One of <code>EQUAL</code>, <code>NOT_EQUAL</code>, <code>IN</code>, <code>NOT_IN</code>, <code>CONTAINS</code>, <code>NOT_CONTAINS</code>, <code>LESS</code>, <code>LESS_EQUAL</code>, <code>GREATER</code>, <code>GREATER_EQUAL</code>, or <code>STARTS_WITH</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8c6847a12c3286aefdb598988aa4045e">
<code>value</code> (string) – Required for all operators except <code>IN</code> and <code>NOT_IN</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb72ff0b504f54ffe7fafa3237a550a19">
<code>values</code> (array of strings) – For <code>IN</code> and <code>NOT_IN</code> only. For example, <code>["Web", "iOS"]</code>. Use instead of <code>value</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e399bbaa0ebdec53a66b042ca0fbf7388">(Optional) <code>negate</code> (boolean) – Inverts the filter, defaults to <code>false</code>. </li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e680b1044991b0cf9d44a39b84f01ab8a">(Optional) <code>dashboard_id</code> – When analyzing an exploration in the context of a dashboard, pass the dashboard ID here (format: <code><number>_<uuid></code>). The backend automatically applies any always-on filter tiles (those with a non-null <code>default_value</code>) at query time without saving. Get this from the  <code>oa_explores_for_dashboard</code> tool. For user-selectable filter tiles, use <code>filters</code> instead. Do not pass explore IDs or experiment IDs here.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec992cf10f723719acd2c4bc8e6c6fa27">(Optional) <code>sampling</code> – Override the sampling configuration for this query. Use this when you want to change sampling behavior (for example, <em>remove sampling and rerun this query</em>, <em>disable sampling</em>, or <em>use faster sampling</em>). The sampling object controls data sampling for query performance. It has the following fields: <ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ee9a9a56632c15933d69e4a71ed9ba7eb">
<code>mode</code> (string) – One of the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e0031c204a89651447c37092deaa16fc1">
<code>FAST</code> – Quick sampling.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3b7137f56e8d923a71c9d8d8d8e14ecc">
<code>PRECISE</code> – Higher accuracy sampling.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0a208efa62bfa4ac11ab3d48755b340f">
<code>DISABLED</code> – No sampling, full scan.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7dee6423f4723b5926af6e873dec2ec3">
<code>PRESET</code> – Use a preset sampling rate, 0-6.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea22f8b6ccf08e51ac98c6b715c3c5b17">
<code>CUSTOM</code> – Specify exact percentage.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2b31a51ad6f6779b62bf83ee25df99ed">(Optional) <code>preset</code> (integer) – For PRESET mode, a value from 0 to 6 where 0 or 1 yields 1% sample, and 2-6 yields 2^(preset-1) percent (for example, preset 6 = 32% sample.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8d5ce48bf4e9850789d3c97d469ed93c">(Optional) <code>rate</code> (number) – For<code> CUSTOM</code> mode, the percentage to sample expressed as a whole number (for example, 5.0 means 5% sample)</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3ad9831e5f2db752d4aaff68a8907f47">(Optional) <code>confidence</code> (number) – Statistical confidence level, currently not used.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5a0855d0eee6e07b910e13893b3d6a80">(Optional) <code>error</code> (number) – Acceptable error margin, currently not used.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e1426cd6d1213e014f46b4df707fee1f4">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb9e98a1359a6b531726dfb1b4bf3cad3"><em>Analyze the "Signup Funnel" exploration for the last 30 days.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed6dce2fafbd8b5f4535ac4e520aefde6"><em>Re-run the "Weekly Active Users" exploration with monthly granularity instead.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e7a79f7d9a246d86d9269888ce703016d"><em>Show me the results of the "Revenue by Region" exploration with sampling disabled.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e820248444214fc242b076ef6c153c899"><em>Analyze the "Checkout Conversion" exploration from the marketing dashboard, filtered to iOS users only.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_create_experiment_scorecard</code> – Creates an experiment scorecard exploration with specified metrics and configuration in Optimizely Analytics.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ed6da1aeae17773967df7dab7a65817a0">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eb0a4043b4ef4690561dd6981629ba18f">Create a new scorecard for an experiment that does not have one yet.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef7d32ed998befdf30571e92fc2b146a5">Build a custom scorecard with specific metrics for an existing experiment.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0be210cffa5f37fa91fe48ceefddee98">Generate a scorecard that can be analyzed or added to an experiment's Explore tab.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ecb4dd9d758a16948ec5cbf3f9d3ac920">Scope a scorecard to a specific cohort or breakdown dimension.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ebc535285eb3604eb620967592eca164b">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="efd2beda0cd9b9982e3983a3a612162ea">
<code>metrics</code> – The metrics to track on the scorecard. This is a list of metric IDs obtained from the <code>oa_find_metrics</code>. tool Each metric ID corresponds to a saved metric entity. At least one metric is required. For example, <code>["metric-id-1", "metric-id-2"]</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1194762fff3026fe249994a37d5c5abc">
<code>experiment</code> – The experiment to create a scorecard for. Can be either the experiment ID (from the <code>oa_find_experiments</code> tool) or the experiment name. If a name is provided, it will be fuzzy-matched to find the experiment.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed7b317d86690aec22c74cfecde2ffaed">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee91ca60c057df46791aa2290bb928bd0">(Optional) <code>filters</code> – Filters to apply to the scorecard to narrow the population. Each filter object has: <code>column_id</code> (an entity reference), <code>operator</code>, and <code>value</code> or <code>values</code>. Multiple filters are combined with AND logic.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eec70267d7ff70f9eea56537e63b3b330">(Optional) <code>actor_dataset</code> – The <code>id</code> field from the dataset object returned by <code>oa_find_datasets</code>. Determines which actor dataset defines the unit of analysis for unique counts.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8bb1472ab59a9ce2e37e8c41c3833930">(Optional) <code>group_by</code> – A breakdown dimension (entity ID from the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool). When provided, results are grouped by this dimension (for example, <code>platform</code>, <code>country</code>, and <code>user segment</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed301a7fcc89a596d91c38d3331cf5444">(Optional) <code>cohort</code> – A cohort ID to apply to the scorecard. Use the <code>oa_find_cohorts</code> tool to discover available cohorts. When specified, the scorecard only includes users in this cohort.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e2cdf3e50341edcdf3e5f6d41a9e081ab">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e0a7199fbcf72e551837cf0ae00ee5f12"><em>Create a scorecard for the "Homepage Redesign" experiment using the "Conversion Rate" and "Revenue per Visitor" metrics.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e67bdca492614c134da363beb88f07d2b">
<em>Build a scorecard for experiment </em><code><em>exp-123</em></code><em> with the "Add to Cart" metric, broken down by country.</em>
</li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ef68f5db52a2d5162c28880c4cd49481d"><em>Create a custom scorecard for the "Checkout Flow" experiment scoped to the "Premium Users" cohort.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_create_exploration_influence</code> – Creates an influence analysis exploration to find what causes or is caused by a target behavior in Optimizely Analytics.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e9ab82b0b93f46bcd539005fcde937f65">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e17286ddfc5eb779b0134ea7238b1bf5e">Analyze what drives or causes a specific outcome. For example, <em>what causes users to purchase?</em>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2e16305131a23c3afda378e6c8bb3ad4">Discover the effects of a target behavior. For example,<em> what happens after users sign up?</em>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eeb4319af611c3cf447dfb980e8179cc7">Reveal temporal relationships between events, cohort membership, or metrics.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e53267fe6edd4dc005a19fff316f2f703">Identify the most influential behaviors or properties leading to a conversion event.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e731b7de77ffc5813a3f8a0b3bc194226">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e1dfbd4566f79b922697a75576b557427">
<code>direction</code> – Analysis direction. Can be one of the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e5fa1ec5e8eccf27bfcd5b3dff9fd983d">
<code>CAUSES</code> – Find what causes the target. Test behaviors happen before target.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eceeb5dcca8f997d2a231c9e35d1653c2">
<code>EFFECTS</code> – Find effects of the target. Test behaviors happen after target.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea00cdff9729bb4ba0282d1635e62ae78">
<code>target_behavior</code> – The behavior to analyze. Must have a <code>type</code> field (<code>DID_EVENT</code>, <code>IN_COHORT</code>, or <code>METRIC</code>) and corresponding data. <ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ea17e753662e0f7bc51aac1d8804f6bed">For <code>DID_EVENT</code> – Include <code>event</code> with <code>dataset_id</code>, <code>event_names</code>, and optional <code>name</code>. </li>
<li data-list-item-id="e64d2341531094509d45c5dca23662742">For <code>IN_COHORT</code> – Include <code>cohort</code> with <code>type</code> (<code>ACTOR_DATASET</code> or <code>COLLECTION</code>) and either <code>actor_dataset_id</code> or <code>collection</code>. </li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8bc945b4ad0cd1ec1ce61b1fadab92fd">For <code>METRIC</code> – Include <code>metric</code> with the metric ID.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3609c0c670bd2d35c5160bf7380ba412">
<code>test_behaviors</code> – The behaviors to test for influence. Must have a <code>type</code> field (<code>DID_EVENT</code>, <code>IN_COHORT</code>, or <code>METRIC</code>) and corresponding data. <ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ef523cea9ab6f2476a68d2a2ad336594e">For <code>DID_EVENT</code> – Include <code>event</code> and <code>test_property</code>. </li>
<li data-list-item-id="e31f271e01dfeb7423d5496907e3f336c">For <code>IN_COHORT</code> – Include <code>cohorts</code> array. </li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea5a8fab0c7cb8e61bb61ba95e4196404">For <code>METRIC</code> – Include <code>metrics</code> array.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8389163211956c5347628cb32782fb9e">
<code>name</code> – A concise, descriptive name for the exploration, intelligently generated by the agent.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e83f94444ffeefd03092877d612f294c8">
<code>time_window</code> – Time window for the temporal relationship. Must have <code>value</code> (integer) and <code>unit</code> (<code>SECOND</code>, <code>MINUTE</code>, <code>HOUR</code>, <code>DAY</code>, <code>WEEK</code>, or <code>MONTH</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec5222d3aa65da2e2669b961b4265e1d8">(Optional) <code>description</code> – A brief description of what the exploration analyzes, intelligently generated by the agent.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e65feaaa965c68368a7da47e335f701ce">(Optional) <code>time_range</code> – Specifies the time range for the analysis. The object must have either a <code>last</code> field for relative ranges or both <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> fields for absolute ranges.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7c5b8244afca4bcae47c8ff2abcaf650">(Optional) <code>time_grain</code> – Specifies the granularity for time-series data. The object has two fields: <code>value</code> (number) and <code>unit</code> (<code>SECOND</code>, <code>MINUTE</code>, <code>HOUR</code>, <code>DAY</code>, <code>WEEK</code>, <code>MONTH</code>, <code>QUARTER</code>, or <code>YEAR</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1f9c2a7245467603964f96291b2f3346">(Optional) <code>actor_dataset</code> – The <code>id</code> field from the dataset object returned by the <code>oa_find_datasets</code> tool. Determines which actor dataset defines the unit of analysis for unique counts. For example, users, accounts, subscriptions, and devices. If not provided, Opal uses the app's default actor dataset.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efbe257d6e0ab7bb3a8f04ccb2abb8f79">(Optional) <code>filters</code> – A list of filters to apply to the exploration. Each filter object has the following: <code>column_id</code> (an entity reference), <code>operator</code>, and <code>value</code> or <code>values</code>. Multiple filters are combined with and logic.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e21014ecde83c58073120df1cf18f6eaa">(Optional) <code>top_n</code> – Limit results to top N most influential items.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e09172197306ac74423a4e8840ef711be">(Optional) <code>chart_config</code> – Chart visualization configuration.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb6164286173a107a426a72fb6c8ed083">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e44d5df40083c327e7b199b20d6518b6d">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ea60dee2cc3bf53afe5dbfeb74996a055"><em>What causes users to complete a purchase within 7 days?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e578074ae2fd06570b671d9313e371edc"><em>Show me what influences churn. What behaviors happen before users cancel their subscription?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="efb607dae2ae9247c9c3524d49b20f5c0"><em>What do users do after signing up? Show me the effects within 30 days.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e071ae96fad183b6df8d3ecf780f11db8"><em>Which events are most influential in driving the "add to cart" event?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_create_exploration_paths</code> – Creates a Path Analysis exploration in Optimizely Analytics to visualize user journeys before and after a focal event.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e44d84d33f535e8ce0c4ffd65360f6ac1">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eee503c8be405b422586d7f98bff7c800">Discover what paths users take before or after a key event. For example, <em>What do users do in the three steps before checkout?</em>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9b3540ee6e1323b0dcbed5868ae562ba">Visualize user journey sequences as a Sankey diagram or table.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8e69dd2de5d27f9b2c7cf01f1dace880">Identify common navigation patterns and drop-off points in a user flow.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ead75b645793571ee683bf950dc75324b">Understand the sequence of actions leading to or following a conversion event.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e4359977b3ace6c224e3397e7d3fe0c58">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ef2bf202bd436a6d85eebe8fde2f327da">
<code>name</code> – A concise, descriptive name for the exploration, intelligently generated by the agent.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e64c4c27d8fd778fb371e8aad62efe5a4">
<code>events</code> – A list of event groups that define the user journey. Each object must have the following three fields: <ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e172efec0e53696c9af040160f6660f15">
<code>name</code> – A descriptive label.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7b2e3513112b5664c6f1cefa58728c34">
<code>dataset_id</code> – The <code>datasetId</code> from <code>JoinableEvent</code> objects. must be the same across all groups.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9d6f2797d2cebdf76d2a865fcb431857">
<code>event_names</code> – Array of event name strings from the <code>oa_find_events</code> tool.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e72d8ec9a3152aac226fde3862a44489b">
<code>focal_event</code> – The name of the event that serves as the focal point of the journey. This must be one of the event names from the <code>events</code> parameter. The path analysis displays what happens before and after this focal event occurs.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e42e2bb567ec45cb77ba35c297a386c91">
<code>steps</code> – Specifies how many steps to show before and after the focal event. Must have <code>before</code> (integer, default 0) and <code>after</code> (integer, default 5) fields. The sum of <code>before</code> + <code>after</code> must be greater than 0. For example, <code>{"before": 2, "after": 3}</code> displays two steps before and three steps after the focal event.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e77efaa7ce41a311bf3e47d376fcfe5f6">
<code>description</code> – A brief, one-sentence description of what the exploration shows, intelligently generated by the agent.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e77df79cbfd45312b929d7d5a0a41bf24">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e476a470278ffe328938c6c2264a572e3">(Optional) <code>time_range</code> – Specifies the time range for the exploration. Accepts relative ranges (for example, <em>last 30 days</em>) or absolute ranges (for example, <em>January 2024 to January 2025</em>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ede8a4a263425bd57243b8e0c2f812979">(Optional) <code>time_grain</code> – Specifies the granularity for time-series data (for example, <em>daily</em>, <em>weekly</em>, or <em>monthly</em>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e72a1ec5db3b6b4273d785031cf81082d">(Optional) <code>actor_dataset</code> – The <code>id</code> field from the dataset object returned by the <code>oa_find_datasets</code> tool. Determines which actor dataset defines the unit of analysis for unique counts.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e643d2bff18b2dfa38c108d34103d5689">(Optional) <code>filters</code> – A list of filters to apply to the exploration. Each filter narrows results to rows where the column matches the given value.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e98d65773fedcb21782d2504b3d4262a5">(Optional) <code>group_by</code> – One or more entity references (from the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool) to group the results by.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e043159ebb34418a1c7b7a6096c2e1292">(Optional) <code>top_n</code> – Maximum number of unique values to show in each step of the path. Defaults to 5. Use this to limit the complexity of the path visualization.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e0da769cb421af4e431653ea8537bb6cd">(Optional) <code>ignore_repeats</code> – Whether to collapse adjacent identical events into a single node in the path. Defaults to <code>false</code>. Set to <code>true</code> to simplify paths where users repeat the same action.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5a1b119c720123106b65035562518b91">(Optional) <code>measure</code> – The measure type. Currently only <code>UNIQUES_CONVERTED</code> (counts unique actors who took the path) is supported. This is the default value.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e083401c8e230215633f3f84ba81ee559">(Optional) <code>chart_config</code> – Chart visualization configuration. For path analysis, the default is a SANKEY diagram. Use this to specify alternative visualizations like <code>{"subType": "TABLE"}</code> to display results as a table.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e7f04106b8b4c10c5cced6c13f08c1bfc">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e60e9850c7ecba75030cecb17993e9ca9"><em>What do users do in the 3 steps before checkout?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e7898b8fcb3b7f68792888532d1997b34"><em>Show me the user journey after the "sign up" event and 5 steps forward.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e136b7da63606adc2a1cd5b3861428069"><em>Create a path analysis showing 2 steps before and 3 steps after the "add to cart" event for the last 30 days.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed19f69355d3de95f8ebbaf74cd074aa5"><em>What paths do users take before reaching the pricing page? Collapse repeated events.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_create_explore</code> – Constructs and saves a <a href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/34053154474509" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Funnel</a>, <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/34053917149581" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Retention</a>, or <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/34052595960077" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Event Segmentation</a> exploration in Optimizely Analytics.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e6dcfae7a3b26568aefb2be5e78ed4eb6">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ec3caeeb6eda4cbb238a8dbbdb97e7076">After you have identified the necessary events using <code>oa_find_events</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ece4463e2730cd257846b97fd24e89d83">After you have identified any entities for grouping using <code>oa_find_entities</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2f75f0ee9d5e1d532218f2df5eac57a8">When you are ready to finalize and save an exploration.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e6d5438e66dfc34d04fb81c0335c9b443">
<div><strong>Parameters</strong></div>
<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e4f57996c30eceaeb9c5de6e0038425ae">
<code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e23fd40b81cc908d6f947c457cd59d6a7">
<code>explore_type</code> – Specifies the type of exploration to create. Available values are <code>FUNNEL_BLOQ</code>, <code>RETENTION</code>, or <code>EVENT_SEGMENT</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee12bf3b42f1c859195522a46d26af72c">
<code>events</code> – A list of event groups that define the exploration.<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e90de39e3f0aba9bc65ecb4fdcecfd4fc">For Funnels, the order of events in this list defines the stage order.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e653427e6fa4b5f7123392df942b24759">For Retention, this list must contain exactly two event groups: the first is the 'initial' event group, and the second is the 'return' event group.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e70de37a379d5dc7123d1c7bb1ac1b1be">For Event Segmentation, this list must contain exactly one event group.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3808f59214b522fd22eeafb51aa3690a">Each event group must contain <code>JoinableEvent</code> objects obtained from the <code>oa_find_events</code> tool.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e35e96e91b54aa29c1b2fbd07e96e159d">(Optional) <code>name</code> – A concise, descriptive name for your exploration. Opal intelligently generates this, but if there is a duplicate name, Opal asks you for a new one.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ecb72907b5a1d32e3560b20fabd129b59">(Optional) <code>description</code> – A brief, one-sentence description of what the exploration shows. Opal intelligently generates one, if you do not provide one.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1f051205e447f1884345fd6c71fc80fe">(Optional) <code>group_by</code>  – The <code>id</code> from a <code>JoinableEntity</code> object (returned by the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool) to group the results. Used when you explicitly request to 'group by' or 'break down by' a specific attribute.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9d6850eeadbc75470c4f51ec8e3e2b84">(Required for <code>EVENT_SEGMENT</code>) <code>measure</code> – The metric to measure for Event Segmentation. Available values are <code>EVENT_COUNT</code>, <code>UNIQUE_ACTOR_COUNT</code>, or <code>AVG_EVENT_BY_ACTOR</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ec1e8f1d0abad19ce2a0b389579221618">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb5a1a3077af54a606ec12fb52df5357a"><em>Create a funnel exploration for users who viewed a product page and then added an item to their cart.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e8966af21e55f817fb0fec24456a8f103"><em>Show me the retention of users who signed up and then returned to make a purchase.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb424fe7754c8a0a74a47cd1e8398dbae"><em>Create an event segmentation report for all 'click' events, grouped by device type.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e71584aced7201ec7317b4f95064d4f74"><em>I want a funnel that tracks 'page_view' of the homepage, followed by 'add_to_cart', and then 'purchase'.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e415787caf2bcdee15f14a540e878eea1"><em>Generate a retention report for users who 'signed_up' and then 'logged_in'.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>oa_create_universal_explore</code> – Creates a Universal exploration to analyze dataset tables by aggregating column values in Optimizely Analytics.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e5b6cbf857decb20d7b0d545bf680994a">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e02ab385357bce20f17e68408ff1ece78">Aggregate a numeric column from a dataset table, for example, total revenue or average subscription value.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e15890e39891689cad3bc3aa2664c8eeb">Count distinct values in a column to understand how many unique entities exist, such as distinct account types.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb4f3fc0a6cb254c9dd3cb7d80867ae28">Track how a column aggregation changes over time by enabling a time-series view.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea3415b120bc69afb4d6e84a133f9b3e9">Break down a dataset metric by a specific attribute, for example, total revenue grouped by plan name.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec38d4e5ec8421f7eff32b247c960b412">Run multiple aggregations in a single exploration, for example, SUM and AVG of the same column simultaneously.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e84fb25a593fa1a4e4d13b5cf137a0822">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e9052e668acd54c5d88710d794324b03f">
<code>name</code> – A concise, descriptive name for the exploration, intelligently generated by the agent.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e969fee3f0d31c53a5b5131d94b41dae0">
<code>description</code> – A brief, one-sentence description of what the exploration shows, intelligently generated by the agent.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e82a14eed81eda6cbc08812dd308849de">
<code>measures</code> – A list of measures to compute. At least one measure is required. Each measure object must have the following fields: <ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e2abb75b21caa954eb16add484ec18ddc">
<code>type</code> (string) – Must be <code>COLUMN_AGGREGATION</code> for this tool. </li>
<li data-list-item-id="e9284e87b5929ceaee00ef60140dff4a5">
<code>aggregation</code> (string) – The aggregation function. One of the following: <ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e277211eef38ce5dfc1ddc3e0488cc275">
<code>COUNT_DISTINCT</code> – Count unique values.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="efef69126ab46a3c9b31d9b036dcee707">
<code>SUM</code> – Sum of values.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6b9f6acb8ae3af1a836916e1ff24195c">
<code>AVG</code> – Average.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed2a8a53437dc3b2087de4f3cd8c839c4">
<code>MIN</code> – Minimum.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eddee814c625e6f8d7a82a0a9500c0eba">
<code>MAX</code> – Maximum.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec5c8173211c4d45b20a34cdc8328fdaa">
<code>COUNT</code> –  Count all rows.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb0a2bc9906efb586c34caca7e8fe421f">
<code>column_id</code> – An entity reference for the column with the following information:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e36588b4fbe6de0b9138bb1597d02d2f6">
<code>entity_id</code> (string) – The <code>id</code> field from an entity returned by the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e97e988db3d834b016464d042fdc82837">(Optional) <code>field_path</code> (string) – Targets a JSON subfield using dot notation (for example, <code>plan.name</code> or <code>revenue</code>). Use <code>field_path</code> only when the entity is a JSON-typed column whose subfields you discovered using the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool. </li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e57cfa4c5dda25fd3ae21dc8d0c6c2e75">(Optional) <code>name</code> (string) – Display name for the measure. If not provided, a default name will be generated.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5e336473f8ad7887dc7fb6c00601c834">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e84996868c55ba535aba6e8a239ebfbeb">(Optional) <code>actor_dataset</code> – The <code>id</code> field from the dataset object returned by the <code>oa_find_datasets</code> tool. Determines which actor dataset defines the unit of analysis for unique counts (for example, <code>users</code>, <code>accounts</code>, <code>subscriptions</code>, and <code>devices</code>). If not provided, Opal uses the app's default actor dataset.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5b90daab8e932345ed29d5cc22d74106">(Optional) <code>attributes</code> – One or more entity references (from the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool) to group the results by. Each element is an entity reference with the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="efab47d4ab21e199155f8af03f2fdd45f"> <code>entity_id</code> (string) – The <code>id</code> field from an entity returned by <code>oa_find_entities</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e41d0c3d6b6088624f728ffb4a80c4d0e">(Optional) <code>field_path</code> (string) – Targets a JSON subfield using dot notation (for example, <code>plan.name</code> or <code>revenue</code>). Use <code>field_path</code> only when the entity is a JSON-typed column whose subfields you discovered using the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee98738c3f58769524dbb40f9c3ccf821">(Optional) <code>filters</code> – A list of filters to apply to the exploration. Multiple filters are combined with and logic. Each filter object has the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ea7c29f9b211c5cd52f77c81465191f49">
<code>column_id</code>  – An entity reference with the following:<ul>
<li data-list-item-id="edd8cad4e7742d508256132dd9e7c2f6f">
<code>entity_id</code> (string) – The <code>id</code> field from an entity returned by the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e577538c5ea6005022e2c5b48cab4a19f">(Optional) <code>field_path</code> (string) – Targets a JSON subfield using dot notation (for example, <code>plan.name</code> or <code>revenue</code>). Use <code>field_path</code> only when the entity is a JSON-typed column whose subfields you discovered through the <code>oa_find_entitie</code> tool.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e43c321bb9eb96bccca1640f7cc6f5e25">
<code>operator</code> (string) – One of <code>EQUAL</code>, <code>NOT_EQUAL</code>, <code>IN</code>, <code>NOT_IN</code>, <code>CONTAINS</code>, <code>NOT_CONTAINS</code>, <code>LESS</code>, <code>LESS_EQUAL</code>, <code>GREATER</code>, <code>GREATER_EQUAL</code>, <code>STARTS_WITH</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ebd71e553a94205aea2732b7ba32101bf">
<code>value</code> (string) – Required for all operators except <code>IN</code> and <code>NOT_IN</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea203fbd72438623f46d0e51e7c6c42bb">
<code>values</code> (array of strings) – For <code>IN</code> and <code>NOT_IN</code> only (for example, <code>["Web", "iOS"]</code>), use instead of <code>value</code>.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eef8bf99c369296d573baeac93d016c3c">(Optional) <code>negate</code> (boolean) – Inverts the filter, defaults to <code>false</code>. </li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6f30ff84aafe8812cfc8d1de23dfb00a">(Optional) <code>show_over_time</code> – Controls whether results are shown as a time series or as a single aggregate value. Defaults to true.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e1ea063a093d880870dc43d78fa257a69">(Optional) <code>time_range</code> – Filters data to a specific time window. The object must have either a <code>last</code> field for relative rangeso4R both <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> fields for absolute ranges. </li>
<li data-list-item-id="e80937f585f6e145c668bc583e29d2d02">(Optional) <code>chart_config</code> – Chart visualization configuration. Common use: set <code>{"subType": "TABLE"}</code> to display results as a table. Other valid <code>subTypes</code> include <code>LINE</code>, <code>BAR</code>, <code>PIE</code>, and <code>HEADLINE</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eb1fd4e28dc22a22f092316b69504b704">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e57bd905011f86db804948ae9b5f4c21b"><em>Show total revenue aggregated from the subscriptions table for the last 30 days, broken down by plan name.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e560bee332745a7150e49d7530c0e688a"><em>How many distinct account types exist in the accounts dataset? Show it as a single number, not over time.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e56c0597f46d25a59c175b1fbcab74f18"><em>Create an exploration that sums revenue and counts distinct customers from the orders table over the past three months, grouped by week.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e1c09614251505a6d403c276881e98e73"><em>Aggregate the average order value from the purchases dataset, filtered to include only orders from the US.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="efcffda1541cef6d9dbf25c36ef2bd2be"><em>Show me the maximum and minimum subscription price from the subscriptions table as a table visualization.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_find_entities</code> – Searches for analytics entities (also known as properties or attributes) based on a natural language query within Optimizely Analytics.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e322529e58123ffe0e8dbcf5a47ebef03">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e1d9a80edb0da7d74b6ed23d9d9355aad">Find specific properties that you want to use for analysis.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e4ed8f14bb329b0cae3975e42b7fe7c12">Identify properties to "group by," "break down by," or analyze "for each" when creating an exploration.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e3751defea7e095a8609428c9fcf8727d">Discover properties related to a specific event that you have already identified using <code>oa_find_events</code>.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="edf341f910fd88e31c41026f63fb05501">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e85fd95abe7c243d1558a53511eaab249">
<code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb1a7153e929133e7968024d8047709c9">
<code>query</code> – A natural language description of the property you are searching for (for example, "country" or "device type").</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2c0ae7b083d3e61d6500adb22a748aa5">(Optional)<strong> </strong><code>event</code> – A <code>JoinableEvent</code> object (returned from the <code>oa_find_events</code> tool) to restrict the search to entities related to that specific event. </li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8ba3913cdbfe0e43f22732a7affd8e5b">(Optional) <code>categories</code> – A list of category IDs to filter results by.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e41f6a51a46f2dd19181455a3f5aea987">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e773782e7dabcd28aa17126831191be84"><em>Find entities related to "country" or "device type."</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="efb693544e96205685ce27b5f7035c84e"><em>What properties can I use to group my 'purchase' events?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e5e17e23c6a08842417f141ea498bf8c9"><em>Show me the entities associated with the 'user signed up' event.</em></li>
<li data-list-item-id="e7a36cad93f59d90cd7f920a00348c761">
<em>I want to break down my funnel by "browser type."</em> </li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>oa_find_events</code> – Searches for and returns a list of analytics events based on a natural language query.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ed59b140594e6264c435189d0c4a71c6f">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ebcc1c76e5d7333165de40e0d2ec12b4a">When you need to identify specific user actions, such as 'user signed up' or 'product added to cart'.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ec1b8f6f78b202dc012fe75466fc28be3">As the initial step in building an analytics exploration, as its output is required by the <code>oa_create_explore</code> tool.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef6bfd2dc9d43bc5e891241cb311349a1">To find events that Opal can use to discover related properties with the <code>oa_find_entities</code> tool.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e439a7601160b24db5b8982f5b497cd89">Find the correct event objects to use as stages in a funnel, initial or return events in a retention report, or events to segment in an event segmentation report.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ed317ee74d4ddc752353cbc9638d50a40">
<strong>Parameters</strong> <ul>

<li data-list-item-id="ee7c74c948f14ad6edc2d5bdb6975324b">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e8a33556c2fbdda716c414b0b3fc1515e">(Optional) <code>actor_dataset</code> – The <code>id</code> field from a dataset object returned by <span class="MathJax_Preview" style="color: inherit;"></span><span id="MathJax-Element-3-Frame" class="mjx-chtml MathJax_CHTML" tabindex="0" style="font-size: 117%; <li data-list-item-id="e08d3626234edfc6f3c9150a6dd1a851c">(Optional) <code>categories</code> – A list of category IDs to filter results by.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e5c816ee51ec89a96b1aeccde01015ac0">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e9569520262c4b64eee59851839f195a5"><em>Find the event for "user signed up."</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e445b32cc63fec86c0c72eb4bdcef0b2a"><em>What are the events related to "product added to cart"?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ecba4a4634c340c5fff5b0d41714bf3ad"><em>Show me the event for when a user "completed checkout."</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e04772a8ea08ac0a9f20f4ab44d8591c3"><em>I need to find events for "page view" and "button click."</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><details><summary><code>oa_find_explores</code> – Helps you find existing saved explorations in Optimizely Analytics by using AI to understand your request and find relevant explorations even if your wording is slightly different from the saved name.</summary><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ea215e86b5b9578578bf0a41f8e04ea81">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul data-indent-level="2">
<li data-list-item-id="ebcb43d3494029eebb11c58c197b3ad9c"><p data-renderer-start-pos="449">You want to locate a previously saved analysis, like a "signup funnel" or "user retention" report.</p></li>
<li data-list-item-id="e6fa8e76d4ef34c2ff7808eaf844eadf8"><p data-renderer-start-pos="551">You are looking for an existing exploration to analyze further.</p></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e6cdbf56df44e880f44e22de43e77323a">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e34f4265d493ffceca9f2e153b5868b50">
<code>query</code> – A natural language description of the event you are searching for (for example, "user signed up").</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e34935ee9e16b0b2fba9f060e382c842c">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e032d2bc7ba160a564968538668eb725d">(Optional) <code>categories</code> – A list of category IDs to filter results by.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="eda067f5bb7b7cc9bd45433f992456f67">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul data-indent-level="2">
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ee4feb9c66c433f52ddcf8c7833e42740"><p data-renderer-start-pos="833"><em>Find my 'signup funnel' exploration.</em></p></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e4049dc0004469a56d3dfcb68c9c88c7f"><p data-renderer-start-pos="875"><em>Are there any saved explorations about user retention?</em></p></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e615d9643fcb5a2afce6cfa5c3e86774b"><p data-renderer-start-pos="935"><em>Show me explorations related to conversion analysis.</em></p></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ed94b8404b76e1c489b7deed34548e459"><p data-renderer-start-pos="993"><em>Can you find the 'Q4 marketing campaign' exploration?</em></p></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></details><h2 id="h_01KVDVD2W8CP5FKXS43Z7SXPGV">Experiment management tools<a class="link-anchor" href="#h_01KVDVD2W8CP5FKXS43Z7SXPGV"></a></h2><details><summary><code>oa_add_explore_to_experiment</code> – Adds an existing exploration to an experiment's Explore Tab in Optimizely Analytics.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e1981a9d0ef84a8cd5c8b5888cc9e1b13">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e0192026a2b01650b0805d2c17206e29a">Add a scorecard or exploration to an experiment's Explore tab for supplementary analysis.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e001e0151ed199e4d57ceab29541acf1f">Attach a saved exploration to an experiment so teams can view it alongside experiment results.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e52f9e7b11ec9f1fccd75ab654209b3f9">Add a newly created scorecard (from the <code>oa_create_experiment_scorecard</code> tool) to an experiment.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ea8d0517934776453a2cb890542d21c20">Enrich an experiment's Explore tab with custom analyses that explain why results occurred.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e9dd8e1b91964bd97ae0c16195aee5d73">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e59b667039d35aa25939319bba64133c7">
<code>explore_id</code> – The unique identifier of the exploration to add. For scorecards from the <code>oa_create_experiment_scorecard</code> tool, use the <code>explore_id</code> field from the response. For saved explores from the <code>oa_find_explores</code> tool, use the <code>id</code> field directly.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ef84d720ad36ba36334b179b924125e60">
<code>experiment</code> – The experiment to add the explore to. Can be either the experiment ID (from the <code>oa_find_experiments</code> tool) or the experiment name. If a name is provided, it will be fuzzy-matched to find the experiment.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e76b7826302ae03e3a05d5a23013f980e">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="edae33de8707cfd49a1ce0b6acd3e4e1a">(Optional) <code>tile_name</code> – A display name for the tile on the experiment's Explore tab. If omitted, the exploration's name is used automatically.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e9b6245189039abe0d263e9799f4b607a">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ec58aab63f77252e67870cb7ff0344ece"><em>Add the scorecard I just created to the "Homepage Redesign" experiment.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e88544fb9bb3923fd31e3a773e476bff9"><em>Attach the "Signup Funnel" exploration to my checkout experiment's Explore tab.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="ecfe173dc8641dd10f13c9f0d6fb50b56">
<em>Add explore </em><code><em>explore-456</em></code><em> to experiment </em><code><em>exp-123</em></code><em> with the tile name "Revenue Breakdown".</em>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_analyze_experiment</code> – Fetches and analyzes the Summary (scorecard) tab for an Optimizely experiment.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e55389297154330f88369a6a7a2a4a422">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e686f6a748e9fdb7950620986a1f8bb0e">View and analyze the results of an experiment, including per-variation statistical data.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee014fe284b602637593a297da2a1e778">Understand whether an experiment's variations achieved statistical significance.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e21b2b41f81b47f0e5c91a109e3bcb7b3">Get a comprehensive analysis of experiment metrics such as conversion rate, revenue, and lift.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ed57b6270523729da2378b1213597d185">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e11e480eb85cbaa274474db97ab890792">
<code>scorecard_explore_id</code> – The explore ID of the experiment scorecard (format: <code><number>_<uuid></code>). Must be the <code>scorecard_explore_id</code> field from the <code>oa_find_experiments</code> tool's response. This is different from the experiment's own <code>id</code> field. Do not pass the experiment <code>id</code> here. iIt does not work. Always call the <code>oa_find_experiments</code> tool first to obtain this value.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e25ad97d490a585ee9bb9568f3448520b">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ecd09694f0411ad65d31206190a562a1f">(Optional) <code>time_range</code> – Overrides the time range for the experiment results. Include when you want a specific time period (for example, <em>show me results for the last 30 days</em>. The object must have either a <code>last</code> field for relative ranges or both <code>start</code> and <code>end</code> fields for absolute ranges.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee2550894c9a1cb717bf72da0ccd6f37e">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e7bebc83b6c243bcfe364d94bf4e50318"><em>Analyze the results of the "Homepage Redesign" experiment.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e27b8ae21223d714ef726fd59bc0bfc54"><em>Show me the experiment scorecard for the "Checkout Flow" test.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e9f7018a53f33de3012a1677753a5a939"><em>What are the results of my latest experiment? Did we reach statistical significance?</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_experiment_explore_tab</code> – Lists the explorations in an experiment's Explore tab in Optimizely Analytics.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ecf5321c566f241888d5c9af851b4de2e">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="ec732fadc7cfefd2f4e590bca0a8fa6e2">View custom analyses attached to an experiment's Explore tab to understand why results occurred.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e5265cfbcb46b171814821b78ebf69773">List all explorations scoped to a specific experiment for further analysis.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e2e070efd5b7379059e466087d6428457">Discover supplementary analyses associated with an experiment before drilling into the data.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e894ac2b8458e1b61f127d5754930919a">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="eaad13a161099ca5af491ca7705fe4ba0">
<code>explores_dashboard_id</code> – The dashboard ID for the experiment's Explore tab (format: <code><number>_<uuid></code>). Must be the <code>explores_dashboard_id</code> field from the <code>oa_find_experiments</code> tool's response. This is a dashboard entity ID scoped to the experiment, not the experiment's own <code>id</code>. If this field is null or missing in the <code>oa_find_experiments</code> response, the experiment has no Explore tab configured.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="ee446b94389fb754be1022856dffde90f">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ef83745d37eabec2613c090699f07add9">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="edd41b746fb1292d67b93bec2ba41796e"><em>Show me the Explore tab for the "Homepage Redesign" experiment.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e0dd53202e8ea1f206fbb0a39b57449fb"><em>What custom analyses are attached to the "Checkout Flow" experiment?</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="eb0f9d83fea1afc8b9a37bc1aeaac8a64"><em>List all explorations on the Explore tab for my latest experiment.</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><details><summary><code>oa_find_experiments</code> – Searches for Optimizely experiments by name in Optimizely Analytics.</summary><div><ul>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e4116dbc8b2ef9c0ca576f7aa2decd759">
<strong>When to use</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e7eed144dab04dd87c125fc54f28ef462">Locate an experiment by name before analyzing its results or viewing its Explore tab.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb5e1afc46bcad44862d80fcd64125203">Look up experiment metadata, including scorecard and Explore tab IDs needed by other tools.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="e32e6c66176a1fa6f86fe75ebe466ac15">List all experiments or search for a specific experiment you want to analyze.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="ee8b5ecf8d4192354e6468e71713a5fe8">
<strong>Parameters</strong><ul>
<li data-list-item-id="e199a9c5db1d88c0105e37f9acd61b9c4">(Optional) <code>query</code> – A natural language search query to find experiments (for example, <em>dragon recommendations</em>, <em>checkout flow test</em>, or <em>homepage redesign</em>). The search uses fuzzy matching on names. Omit or pass an empty string to list all experiments.</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eb68c3a8811feaa122f4c834c1004fd0b">(Optional) <code>appid</code> – The ID of your Optimizely Analytics application for context. Opal uses the <code>appid</code> from your system context if available, or explicitly asks you for this value. You can often find it in the URL of your Optimizely Analytics project (signified by <code>?app=</code>).</li>
<li data-list-item-id="eec7dc7a0b9d6753f9db12119da6fe587">(Optional) <code>categories</code> – A list of category IDs to filter results by. When provided, only results that belong to at least one of the specified categories are returned. Use the <code>oa_list_categories</code> tool to discover available categories and their IDs. Category filtering is handled entirely by this parameter. Do not include category names or references to categories in the <code>query</code> parameter. If the request is solely about filtering by category, use a broad <code>query</code> such as an empty string.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li class="wysiwyg-list-bold" data-list-item-id="e2a5302b5f73835f471ca79e96ec403c4">
<strong>Example prompts</strong><ul>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e8e22669ab3d5660c56653ea6335f8095"><em>Find the "Homepage Redesign" experiment.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e658d26f0bf34ea688b7570cd644b1108"><em>List all my experiments.</em></li>
<li class="ck-list-marker-italic" data-list-item-id="e5f0a30a4b976292730b484b0b5b58451"><em>Search for experiments related to "checkout flow".</em></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul></div></details><div class="note"><p>If you use Opti ID, administrators can turn off generative AI in the Opti ID Admin Center. See <a href="/hc/en-us/articles/36402464751501" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Turn generative AI off across Optimizely applications</a>.</p></div>
